summary: Iteration 4 — Chat file attachments (GridFS): 20/20 backend pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iter4_attachments.py, plus 27/27 prior tests (iter3 + iter2 baseline). Full frontend UI end-to-end verified: paperclip attach button, pending-file chip with remove button, PDF & PNG upload flows, file message bubbles with FileText icon + Download icon, image thumbnails, 10 MB client-side guard toast, and text-only regression all working. WebSocket push of attachment message confirmed. GridFS bucket 'chat_attachments' is properly configured; download endpoint streams byte-identical files with correct Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1446 lines. Highly recommend splitting into routers (auth, tutors, bookings, admin, messaging, attachments, attendance, email). Not blocking but maintenance-heavy.

MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES check reads the entire file into memory before size validation (`data = await file.read()` then `len(data) > MAX`). For 10 MB this is fine, but consider streaming validation via file.file.tell() or checking Content-Length header first to reject early — avoids buffering 10 MB from malicious clients.

Attachment auth on download does an extra DB round-trip: db.messages.find_one({'attachment.id': file_id}). Consider adding an index: `db.messages.create_index('attachment.id', sparse=True)` for scale.

Filename in Content-Disposition is not sanitized/encoded — a filename containing '"' or non-ASCII could break the header. Use RFC 5987 encoding (`filename*=UTF-8''...`) or werkzeug.utils.secure_filename.

No virus/mime-sniffing on upload — trusts client-declared Content-Type. A malicious client can upload a .exe with content_type='application/pdf'. Consider python-magic to verify actual bytes vs claimed MIME.

GridFS orphan cleanup: if `_verify_can_message` throws AFTER `fs.upload_from_stream` completes, the file would already be persisted. Currently _verify runs BEFORE upload (line 859 — good), but if an exception fires between upload and insert_one, we leak the GridFS blob. Wrap in try/except and delete on failure.
WebSocket broadcast doesn't remove dead sockets on send failure (still an iter3 finding). Not user-visible but leaks memory over time.
Frontend Messages.jsx now 233 lines with three separate render branches (image / file / text) inside the same JSX — extract a MessageBubble subcomponent for readability.
seed_data_creation: Created ~4 stranger accounts (stranger_tutor_*, stranger_student_*) for 403 auth tests, and ~6 attachment messages (PDFs + PNGs) between Demo Student <-> Demo Tutor. Harmless demo history.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter4 backend suite at /app/backend/tests/test_iter4_attachments.py — run with `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> python -m pytest backend/tests/test_iter4_attachments.py -o addopts='' -v`. Uses pytest.iter4_pdf_id / iter4_png_id module state to chain upload→download tests, so keep addopts='' (no xdist). GridFS bucket name is 'chat_attachments'. Frontend accept list matches backend ALLOWED_ATTACHMENT_TYPES exactly. WebSocket test uses threading to upload in parallel with async ws.recv() — pattern works reliably.
